newsitem.title: USA: EMC sees margin, pricing improvements in Q4.
newsitem.headline: EMC sees margin, pricing improvements in Q4.

text.p: EMC Corp said on Tuesday it experienced significant improvements during the fourth quarter in its gross and operating margins, as pricing pressure continued to moderate.
The company also said that, during the fourth quarter, it extended its worldwide market share gains over International Business Machines Corp in mainframe storage capacity.

"The fourth quarter of 1996 was by far the most successful quarter in EMC's 17-year history in terms of market and financial performance, with a dramatic upturn in our rate of growth and profitability," Michael Ruettgers, EMC president and chief executive officer said. "The explosive growth of our open storage business was again a major factor."

Ruettgers said revenue from open storage was more than 150 percent higher in the fourth quarter compared with the fourth quarter of 1995, with record demand in both the direct and indirect selling channels.
The company reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.50 per share compared with $0.26 per share in the year-ago quarter.
International sales grew 30 percent sequentially, the company said. It said international sales comprised 44 percent of EMC's total revenues in the fourth quarter.
EMC also said its performance in the quarter was helped by the early availability of its new generation of Symmetrix Integrated Cached Disk Array systems, used for storage.
"We began shipping these new systems in the fourth quarter," Reuttgers said. "Customer response has been tremendous."
